items.title: Oral nutrition supplement interventions show short-term benefits in patient outcomes at low cost for older adults
items.text: A systematic review published in the journal Value in Health by Amarsinh Desai, Ph.D., Olivia M. Dong, Ph.D., and colleagues examines the health and economic effects of oral nutrition supplements in older adults, most with or at risk of malnutrition. The researchers found that oral nutrition supplement use, often as part of broader nutrition interventions, was generally associated with modest short-term improvements in health outcomes and was cost-effective or cost-saving, with economic benefits largely driven by reductions in health care resource utilization, such as fewer hospitalizations.

items.title: The same gene that helps define neuron identity may also balance developing brain circuits
items.text: A gene that helps set a neuron's identity also affects how many inputs it receives from other neurons. New research led by neuroscientists at King's College London finds that the molecules neurons use to wire together in the developing mouse brain depend on the role these neurons will play in the adult. The connections these neurons form also depend on how electrically active they are during development.
